newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures end mixed as dollar sags.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures end mixed as dollar sags.

text.p: IMM currency futures ended pit trading mixed on Thursday as the dollar sagged and major funds continued a week of fast-paced cash cross action.
The dollar gave up ground versus the mark and yen on cash markets, hurt by broad-based selling of Treasuries.

"What we're doing is unwinding the strength we had earlier in the week, which was not based on fundamentals at all," said one currencies analyst. "That's not really surprising. (The dollar) ran up on nothing, just a bandwagon to buy it, with vocal support from European officials, but jawboning is not any sustained basis for dollar strength."

Selling of December sterling was heavy in the morning, then slowed as attempts to drive the contract to new lows stalled. "It looks like the last wave, or hopefully the last wave" of sterling sales, one trader said.

December yen rallied in the morning, then leveled off after remarks by Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of the Japanese Finance Ministry's International Finance Bureau, that were variously interpreted. No clear direction was gleaned, although one trader noted that the official's refusal to set a ceiling for dollar-yen may mean Japan wants the yen to go lower.
"He made comments to the effect that they're not changing their dollar policy, but he also said he didn't expect the yen to weaken too much. So I think he wants it both ways," one trader said.

At the end of pit trading, December yen were up $0.000053 at $0.008911, marks were up 0.0038 at $0.6452, Swiss francs were up $0.0039 at $0.7619, sterling was off 0.0108 at $1.6320, Canadian dollars were off $0.0022 to $0.7370, Australian dollars were off $0.0010 to $0.7979 and Mexican pesos were unchanged at $0.125950.
